title: World Currencies & Timezones
description: 40 original questions matching countries to their currencies, symbols, and fascinating global timezone facts.
author: QuizRooms

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Japan (symbol ¥)?
questions.explanation: The Japanese yen (JPY) is the third-most traded currency in the foreign exchange market.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of the United Kingdom (symbol £)?
questions.explanation: The pound sterling is the world's oldest currency still in continuous use.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Switzerland and Liechtenstein?
questions.explanation: The Swiss franc (CHF) is widely regarded as a safe-haven currency.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of the United Arab Emirates?
questions.explanation: The UAE dirham (AED) has been pegged to the US dollar since 1997.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Saudi Arabia?
questions.explanation: The Saudi riyal (SAR) is subdivided into 100 halalas.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Kuwait — the highest-valued currency unit per 1 unit in the world?
questions.explanation: One Kuwaiti dinar (KWD) is worth over 3 US dollars.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Egypt?
questions.explanation: Locally called 'gineih', the Egyptian pound is divided into 100 piastres.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of South Korea (symbol ₩)?
questions.explanation: The Bank of Korea issues the won (KRW).

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of China (officially Renminbi, symbol ¥)?
questions.explanation: Renminbi ('people's currency') is the official name, while yuan is the primary unit.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of India (symbol ₹)?
questions.explanation: The ₹ symbol combines the Devanagari 'र' and Latin 'R'.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Brazil (symbol R$)?
questions.explanation: The real (BRL) replaced the cruzeiro real in 1994.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Mexico?
questions.explanation: The Mexican peso was the first currency in the world to use the '$' sign.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Turkey (symbol ₺)?
questions.explanation: The Turkish lira (TRY) is used across Turkey and Northern Cyprus.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Thailand (symbol ฿)?
questions.explanation: The baht is also a traditional Thai unit of mass for gold.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Malaysia?
questions.explanation: Ringgit means 'jagged' in Malay, referring to the serrated edges of old Spanish silver dollars.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Indonesia?
questions.explanation: The rupiah (IDR) is issued by Bank Indonesia.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Vietnam (symbol ₫)?
questions.explanation: The Vietnamese dong (VND) has been Vietnam's currency since 1978.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of South Africa?
questions.explanation: The rand takes its name from the gold-rich Witwatersrand ridge.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Poland?
questions.explanation: Złoty literally means 'golden' in Polish.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Sweden?
questions.explanation: Sweden voted against adopting the euro in a 2003 referendum.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Norway?
questions.explanation: Norway is not an EU member and uses the krone (NOK).

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Czechia (Czech Republic)?
questions.explanation: Koruna means 'crown' in Czech.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Hungary?
questions.explanation: The forint takes its name from Florence's medieval gold florin.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Nigeria introduced the naira (NGN) in 1973 to replace the Nigerian pound.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Morocco?
questions.explanation: The Moroccan dirham (MAD) is issued by Bank Al-Maghrib.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Peru?
questions.explanation: Sol means 'sun' in Spanish, honoring the Inca sun god Inti.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Philippines (symbol ₱)?
questions.explanation: Locally called 'piso', it reflects centuries of Spanish-Pacific trade.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Botswana?
questions.explanation: Pula means 'rain' in Setswana — a blessing in the Kalahari.

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: Taka (BDT) was introduced after Bangladesh's independence in 1972.

questions.prompt: Which country uses the world's earliest time zone (UTC+14), making its Line Islands the first inhabited place to greet each New Year?
questions.explanation: Kiribati shifted the International Date Line eastward in 1995 so the whole nation shared one calendar day.

questions.prompt: Which country spans the most total time zones on Earth (12) when including its overseas departments and territories?
questions.explanation: From French Polynesia (UTC−10) to Wallis and Futuna (UTC+12), France spans 12 time zones.

questions.prompt: Which country spans the most contiguous time zones across one continuous landmass (11)?
questions.explanation: Russia stretches from UTC+2 in Kaliningrad to UTC+12 in Kamchatka.

questions.prompt: Which major Asian country uses a single official national time zone (UTC+8) despite spanning 5 geographical time zones?
questions.explanation: All of China observes Beijing Time (UTC+8).

questions.prompt: Which country famously uses a unique 45-minute timezone offset: UTC+05:45?
questions.explanation: Nepal Standard Time is 15 minutes ahead of India Standard Time (UTC+05:30).

questions.prompt: What is India Standard Time's offset from Coordinated Universal Time (UTC)?
questions.explanation: India uses a single half-hour offset across the entire country.

questions.prompt: Which town in London defines the reference meridian for Greenwich Mean Time (GMT / UTC+0)?
questions.explanation: The Royal Observatory Greenwich became the global zero-longitude reference in 1884.

questions.prompt: How many degrees of longitude correspond to a 1-hour difference in solar time?
questions.explanation: 360 degrees divided by 24 hours equals 15 degrees per hour.

questions.prompt: Which country adopted the Euro most recently on January 1, 2023 (becoming the 20th Eurozone member)?
questions.explanation: Croatia replaced the Croatian kuna with the euro in 2023.

questions.prompt: Which US state does NOT observe Daylight Saving Time (alongside Hawaii)?
questions.explanation: Most of Arizona stays on Mountain Standard Time year-round (the Navajo Nation does observe DST).

questions.prompt: What is the official currency of Romania?
questions.explanation: Leu means 'lion' in Romanian.
